title: Junior Developer - AI-Augmented Product & Tooling Team
job_title: Junior Developer - AI-Augmented Product & Tooling Team
description: USD Pay · Long-Term · Philippines What We're Building We build AI-powered consumer products, custom developer tooling, and client solutions across multiple verticals: AI image and video generation — a mobile and web app that transforms photos into stylized artwork using generative AI. Single Flutter codebase, Firebase backend, multiple AI model integrations. Game development — interactive experiences with structured world-building and AI-assisted content generation. Prompt research and skills tooling — we built a package manager for AI agent prompts and skills that detects your repo's tech stack and ranks results accordingly. We research how prompts perform across different models, build reusable skill packages that any AI coding agent can load, and maintain a catalog of 30+ skills covering everything from security review to prompt quality self-assessment. This isn't a side project — it's a core product. MCP and agent workflow research — we actively research and build integrations using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and other emerging standards that reduce friction between developers and AI agents. We've built coordination servers that let multiple agents reserve files, message each other, and avoid conflicts. We've built tmux-based orchestration so developers can run 3-5 AI agents in parallel. When a new protocol, tool, or workflow pattern emerges, we evaluate it against real work and adopt or build what's missing. Code quality tooling for agentic development — AI agents write a lot of code fast. The bottleneck isn't speed, it's confidence. We built compiler-integrated mutation testing and code quality metrics in Rust and TypeScript — tools that use each language's native AST parser so agents and developers can trust that generated code actually works. These aren't standalone research projects; they're the quality backbone that makes high-velocity agentic development safe. Infrastructure and DevOps — Kubernetes clusters, CI/CD pipelines, private networking, infrastructure-as-code across all projects. How We Work We follow a pattern that defines the team culture: see a gap ? research what's available ? build it or adopt the best option ? ship it ? share it with the team. We needed mutation testing tuned to our languages — generic linters couldn't handle Rust's error propagation or TypeScript's union types correctly. So we built compiler-integrated tools that use each language's native AST parser. We needed AI coding agents to coordinate without stepping on each other's files. So we built an MCP coordination server and a tmux orchestrator. We needed an issue tracker that works inside AI agent sessions. So we ported an open-source one to Rust and integrated it into the workflow. We needed to understand why some prompts waste tokens and others don't. So we built a prompt quality analyzer that extracts your messages from session logs, rates them, and shows you exactly where you're losing efficiency. A new AI model drops on OpenRouter — by the end of the week, someone on the team has tested it against our workflow and reported back. A new MCP server appears on GitHub — someone's already evaluated whether it solves a real problem for us. A new ---------- tool shows up on Twitter — someone's tried it in a real session. This isn't a scheduled R&D activity. It's how the team operates. The internal tools are mostly Rust and Go. The products are Flutter and TypeScript. Client work varies — we recently picked up a Drupal project, and the expectation was that the team could ramp on an unfamiliar framework in a day using AI-assisted exploration. That's the skill we hire for. What Makes This Team Different Every developer works alongside AI coding agents as core workflow — not as an experiment. You'll have: 5 AI coding runtimes at your workstation (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor) 30+ custom agent skills covering security, testing, architecture, code review, and prompt quality analysis Multi-agent coordination via MCP so you can run several AI assistants on different tasks simultaneously without file conflicts Automated quality gates (mutation testing, code metrics, security scanning, bug scanning) that give you confidence in AI-generated code before it hits review Prompt research tools that help you measure and improve how effectively you communicate with AI agents We don't just use these tools. We build them, research the protocols behind them, improve them, and expect every developer to have opinions about what works and what doesn't. What We Expect From You You experiment before you're told to. When a new AI model, CLI tool, MCP server, or workflow appears — on Twitter , Hacker News, a ---------- , wherever — your instinct is to install it and try it. Not bookmark it. Not wait for a tea ---------- eting. Try it, form a view, share what you found. You assess your own work. We have tools that analyze prompt quality, code review effectiveness, and development patterns. You're expected to run them on yourself, identify your own anti-patterns, and fix them. Nobody will chase you to do this. You learn by doing, not by reading. Our onboarding gives you access to the full environment on day one. We expect you to explore it. Open things, break things, ask questions when you're stuck — but try first. If we hand you a framework you've never seen before, the expectation is that you and your AI agents figure it out together — fast. You communicate early, not late. Blocked for 30 minutes? Say something. Found a problem nobody mentioned? Flag it. A process doesn't make sense? Push back. Silence is the only wrong answer. You follow through. When you pick up a task, you own it until it's done — including tests, docs, and letting the team know it's complete. What the Work Looks Like Build and ship features in Flutter (Dart) and Firebase Functions (TypeScript) Contribute to internal Rust and Go tooling as you grow into the stack Research and evaluate new AI models, MCP integrations, and developer tools Integrate AI models for image generation, video generation, and content moderation Pick up unfamiliar frameworks for client projects using AI-assisted exploration Conduct peer reviews that actually catch problems — not rubber stamps Evaluate new tools, models, and workflows as they emerge and share findings with the team Run self-assessments on your development practices and discuss results at standups Improve the team's engineering standards — our docs are living documents, not commandments Tech Stack Products: Flutter (Dart) — iOS, Android, web from one codebase Firebase Functions Gen 2, Node.js 25, TypeScript Firestore, Cloud Storage, Stripe OpenAI API, Google Gemini, Vision API Internal Tooling: Rust — mutation testing, code quality metrics, issue tracking, bug scanning Go — AI skill package management, multi-agent orchestration, MCP coordination servers Infrastructure: Kubernetes, Forgejo (self-hosted git), Jenkins CI/CD Ansible, OpenTofu, Semaphore, SAST/DAST and other security tooling Lefthook, oxlint, Prettier, Spectral, Checkov, gitleaks, semgrep You don't need to know all of this on day one. You need to be the kind of person who starts exploring it on day one. Schedule The team currently works 4pm–12am PHT (Manila time), but other schedules overlapping with US Eastern business hours can also be accommodated. We work this window as a team. As we grow, we plan to introduce flexible scheduling as additional teams are creating with other schedules. Compensation We're a bootstrapped startup pre-launch, looking for junior developers who are hungry to build real skills on real products. Starting compensation is junior-rate USD, paid via OnlineJobs.ph / Payoneer. Compensation scales once we launch and have revenue — early tea ---------- mbers who prove themselves will be first in line for increases. What you get: Production experience shipping AI consumer products with professional engineering practices Daily hands-on experience with AI coding tools and internal Rust/Go tooling most developers never touch Exposure to prompt engineering research, MCP integrations, and agent workflow design Direct mentorship on a small team — no layers between you and decisions USD income with growth tied directly to company growth A real voice in how the team works and what tools we build next How to Apply Step 1: Pick any AI coding tool you haven't used before — Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, RooCode, Kiro, GitHub Copilot, anything. Spend 30 minutes using it on a small task (a personal project, a tutorial, a three.js game, a port of a popular utility into Rust, a throwaway script — doesn't matter). Step 2: Send your application with: What you built with the AI tool — what you tried, what surprised you, whether you'd use it again. A few sentences is fine. We don't care which tool or whether you liked it. We care that you tried it and formed a view. A project you've built that you're proud of (link or description) Your experience with Flutter, TypeScript, Rust or similar Your availability (full-time or part-time) Your expected monthly rate (USD)

We serve agency owners and in-house performance marketers who need to connect ad spend to revenue outcomes without the guesswork. The platform is in active build across multiple workstreams — ad account analytics, CRM and lead management, page and funnel builder, conversion mapping, and an AI assistant layer (MODA) that ties it all together. This is a ground-floor opportunity to shape a product that sits at the intersection of advertising data, automation, and applied AI. ## The Role We're hiring a full-stack developer whose default mode is building with AI — not just using it as a novelty feature, but treating it as core infrastructure. You'll be working across the Moredemand platform in Next.js, shipping features end-to-end from spec to production. This is a hands-on building role. You'll receive detailed specs and PRDs with user stories, business logic, and acceptance criteria (written in Gherkin). You won't be guessing what to build — but you will need to make smart technical decisions about how to build it, and move fast doing so. You'll be working alongside an existing small dev team and reporting directly to the founder. ## What You'll Be Doing - Building and shipping production features across the Moredemand platform in Next.js (App Router, Server Components, Server Actions) - Integrating AI/LLM capabilities throughout the product — not bolted-on chat widgets, but intelligent features woven into the user experience (triage, analysis, recommendations, natural language querying, content generation) - Working with the Google Ads, Meta Ads, and analytics APIs to ingest, normalise, and surface advertising data - Building CRM-style interfaces — database views, saved filters, inline actions, dynamic tables, drag-and-drop workflows - Developing the page/funnel builder module with overlay and popup elements - Implementing a consent management layer and data-triggered qualification rules - Writing clean, testable code against Gherkin acceptance criteria provided in each spec - Using Claude Code, Cursor, or equivalent AI-assisted development tooling as a core part of your workflow — not occasionally, but as standard practice - Shipping iteratively with a bias toward working software over perfect abstractions ## What We're Looking For - Strong production experience with Next.js 14+ (App Router, not Pages Router) — this is non-negotiable - Proven ability to build with LLM APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI, or similar) — prompt engineering, structured outputs, tool use, streaming responses, RAG patterns - Comfortable across the full stack: React/TypeScript on the front end, Node.js/serverless on the back end, PostgreSQL or equivalent relational database - Experience integrating third-party APIs — particularly ad platforms, CRMs, or data-heavy SaaS integrations - Ability to work from a detailed spec and translate user stories and business logic into shipped features without requiring architectural hand-holding - Familiarity with AI-assisted development workflows (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, or similar) and the discipline to review and own what the tools produce - Test-driven mindset — you understand Gherkin acceptance criteria and write code that satisfies them - Clean component architecture, sensible state management, and an instinct for UI that feels fast and responsive - Self-directed and reliable in a remote, async-first environment — you ship, you communicate, you don't disappear ## Tech Environment - Next.js (App Router), React, TypeScript - Tailwind CSS - PostgreSQL - Anthropic Claude API (primary LLM layer) - Google Ads API, Meta Marketing API - Vercel deployment - Claude Code / AI-assisted development as standard workflow - Spec-first methodology — block-based architecture, PRDs with Gherkin acceptance criteria, no code or DB schema in specs ## Bonus Points - Experience building SaaS platforms for marketers or agencies - Familiarity with advertising data models (campaigns, ad groups, keywords, conversion actions, attribution) - Experience with real-time dashboards, charting libraries (Recharts, D3), or data visualisation - Background in building form/page builders or drag-and-drop interfaces - Understanding of FCA-regulated or compliance-sensitive product environments - Contributions to open-source or a portfolio of shipped SaaS products ## How to Apply Send the following: 1. A short Loom (under 3 minutes) walking through a Next.js project you built — show the code, explain the decisions, highlight any AI/LLM integration 2. A brief description of how you currently use AI tooling in your development workflow — what tools, how often, and what you trust them with vs. what you don't 3. One example of a feature you shipped from spec to production, and what the spec looked like vs. what you delivered 4. Your availability (hours per week or full-time) and rate (hourly, daily, or monthly) No agencies. No CVs padded with frameworks you used once on a tutorial. Show the work.

title: Vibe Coder (FULL TIME)
description: Summary About the role I run a growing portfolio of online media businesses powered by custom AI tooling. I'm looking for a Vibe Coder / Prompt Engineer to take ownership of building, extending, and maintaining the AI-powered tools, landing pages, and prompt systems that run the operation. This is not a traditional software engineering role — you'll work almost entirely through AI coding assistants (Claude, Cursor, Codex — I provide access) to ship features, fix bugs, and build new products. I don't care how you type the code; I care that what you ship works when I open it. What you'll do — three areas: 1. Tools & platform. Build and maintain our internal AI production tools end-to-end — front end, backend, AI API integration, deployment. Ship features, fix bugs, keep things stable as we scale, and build integrations with third-party services (image/video generation, TTS, YouTube Data API, Google Drive). Stack is React, TypeScript, Node, tRPC, Tailwind — you should be comfortable working in that even if the AI writes most of the lines, and understand what the code does and how to fix it when it breaks. 2. Landing pages & analytics. Build clean, fast, conversion-focused landing pages and webstores, and a centralized analytics dashboard — a single pane of glass pulling webstore metrics (revenue, conversion, AOV, funnel drop-off) and YouTube metrics (views, CTR, watch time, revenue per channel) so the team has real-time visibility without checking five platforms. 3. Prompt engineering. Write, test, and refine prompts for image, video, and text generation as a core, ongoing part of the work, and bake prompt systems into the tools. What I'm looking for: You take a goal and return a working, deployed, tested product — not "done on my machine" or "sitting in a branch." If you tell me it's tested, it's tested. You're a proactive self-starter. Nobody will write you a detailed spec. You'll get a Loom or a message describing what's needed and figure out the rest. If something breaks, you investigate before being asked. If you spot a better way, you flag it and build it. You communicate status honestly — "done and live here," or "80% done, blocked on X, here's my plan." Overstating what's finished is the fastest way to not work with me. You move fast — features in hours, not days — and hit deadlines, or flag early if you can't. Nice to have (not required): analytics dashboards / YouTube & Google Analytics APIs; Stripe and e-commerce flows; prompt engineering for image/video models; Drizzle ORM or other TypeScript-first stacks. Hours & working style: Remote, full-time. We move fast and I need you reachable and actively working during core hours, CET time zone. I care about responsiveness and shipped results, not clock-watching. Compensation: Base Retainer (Months 1-3): $600 USD / month Base Retainer (Month 4+): $800 USD / month (based on performance) Maximum Monthly Earnings: Up to $2,000 USD / month (base + bonuses) Paid monthly via Wise. All tools, AI subscriptions, and API credits are covered by me; you provide your own computer and internet. Process: a short trial task so I can see how you actually work, then ongoing engagement for strong performers. To apply — follow these exactly (applications that don't are deleted unread): Start your message with the word "AVATAR" so I know you read this. Send 2–3 links to tools you have personally built AND deployed — live URLs I can open and use right now, not just GitHub repos. For one of them, tell me what you built, how much of it you built yourself, what tools you used, and how long it took. In two sentences: what's one thing you shipped that you're proud of, and what was the hardest part? Which AI coding tools do you use day to day? Optional but it helps you stand out: include a short Loom (under 5 minutes) on why you're a great fit. I weigh applicants who do this more heavily — it shows initiative and lets me see how you communicate. No generic cover letters. Show me you read this. I reply only to applications that follow the steps above.

description: Title: AI-Augmented Laravel + Vue 2 Developer / Engineer (EU property-tech, remote) Role We are looking for a strong, reliable engineer who likes to move fast with AI tools and still ships carefully. You are expected to use coding assistants to speed up analysis and implementation, but you treat generated output as draft work: clarify scope, plan the change, verify behaviour, keep diffs small, and prove changes with sensible and thorough checks and testing before review. This role is a great fit if you like turning requirements into a short plan, using AI where it helps, keeping changes easy to review, and checking your work before you ask for feedback. It is not a fit if you want to ship large unreviewed blocks of AI-generated code. What you will do - Deliver scoped changes on a mature Laravel + Vue 2 codebase using AI-assisted methods safely. - Open merge requests with clear descriptions, scoped commits, and tests where applicable. - Communicate in writing about plan, trade-offs, and verification steps. Requirements - Demonstrable AI-assisted workflow in real product work (you can explain it concretely). - Comfortable working in Laravel in a larger codebase, including reading and navigating existing code you did not write yourself. - Comfortable with Vue 2 in production, or strong Vue experience with a clear plan to work within Vue 2 patterns in this codebase. - Comfortable with Blade templates and web security (escaping, CSRF, safe handling of user input). - Solid Git habits: branches, scoped commits, merge request workflow. - Written English strong enough for async work with EU stakeholders. - Ideally 4 to 6 hours overlap per workday with CET business hours (Monday to Friday). Please state your timezone and the CET window you can reliably cover each workday. Nice to have - AI-assisted work on legacy codebases (careful refactors, incremental upgrades, tenant-scoped features). - Laravel Mix / Webpack and Docker-based local builds. - Multi-tenant SaaS experience. Trial (before any production access) We run a mini-trial on a sandbox repository that mirrors our stack patterns but contains no production code or customer data. Timebox is about 4 to 6 hours, agreed upfront. You may use AI tools during the trial, but you must not paste secrets, customer data, production logs, or private business information into external tools. You must be able to explain and defend everything you submit. How to apply (English, no template letters) 1) Your current AI-assisted workflow: how you scope prompts, verify output, and prevent scope creep. 2) One example where an AI tool gave a wrong or risky suggestion. How did you catch it? 3) Either (A) walk us through one concrete merge request or commit you authored where AI was your primary tool: what you prompted, what came back, and what you changed before merge, or (B) if you cannot share a link, describe your first 30 minutes on an unfamiliar legacy Laravel/Vue task before you edit code. 4) How do you keep AI-assisted changes small and reviewable in a legacy monolith? 5) Multi-tenant safety: what checks would you do before changing a query that returns tenant-owned records? 6) What information must never be pasted into external AI tools? Name categories, not examples from real projects. Do not apply if - You are not the person who will do the work. - You ship AI output without verification. - You cannot describe your workflow concretely. - You only have Vue 3 experience and cannot commit to Vue 2 patterns in this codebase. - You would paste secrets, production logs, or customer data into external tools.

title: iOS & Android App Developer
description: Senior Mobile Developer / Development Team — iOS & Android Full-Time Engagement  •  Long-Term  •  Start to Finish + Ongoing Maintenance IMPORTANT: This posting is for a long-term, full-time engagement — not a one-off project. We are building a complete consumer mobile platform from scratch and need a committed development partner for the full build lifecycle and beyond. Please only apply if you are available full-time and interested in a multi-month engagement with continued maintenance responsibilities after launch. Overview We are a US-based startup building a consumer mobile application for iOS and Android. The platform combines social discovery, real-time location features, and community scheduling — targeting an active adult demographic in major US cities. Full concept details are shared under NDA with shortlisted candidates. We have a completed Figma design, a detailed product specification, and UI mockups ready to hand off. We are ready to begin immediately and are looking for a technical partner who will own this from day one through launch and beyond — not a one-off contractor. Note: We are intentionally keeping the specifics of the concept vague in this posting to protect our IP. Shortlisted candidates will receive a full product specification document under NDA before the interview stage. What We Are Building The app has the following core functional areas. Details are intentionally high-level — full specification shared under NDA at the shortlist stage: User accounts and onboarding • Multi-step onboarding with media upload and user preference configuration • Optional identity verification via a third-party service • Profile badge system with free and paid tiers • Peer review and rating system Content and user discovery • Grid-based browse interface with expandable detail views • Feed-based discovery with filter and sort • Real-time interactive map view with live status indicators — a signature feature • Username search User-generated listings and scheduling • Users can create, manage, and publish listings • Request-to-join flow with host approval controls • Architecture must support high concurrent participation per listing • Real-time status changes reflected on the map • Granular host controls over messaging permissions Activity feed • Social feed of user activity • User activity logging with tagging and feed posting • Likes, comments, shares on feed posts Messaging • Gated in-app direct messaging • Chat access controlled by specific in-app conditions • Full-featured messaging UI • Push notifications throughout Trust and reputation system • Optional post-interaction rating and review • Blind mutual rating system • Trust and reputation system displayed on profiles • Rating eligibility tied to verified participation User safety and controls • Block, report, and content moderation controls • User preference and safety filtering • Location privacy controls • Visibility controls for users Navigation • Multi-tab bottom navigation covering the core feature areas • Full navigation spec provided to shortlisted candidates Monetization infrastructure (architecture only at launch) None of the following are active at launch. All must be architected in from day one so they can be switched on without a rebuild. This is a non-negotiable requirement. • Payment processing via Stripe — integrated but dormant at launch, activatable for subscriptions, one-time purchases, and transaction fees • Tiered user badge system — free and paid badge types must be supported in the data model from day one; new badge types must be addable without schema changes • Ad slot architecture — designated injectable ad placements in the feed (between posts), at the top and bottom of key screens, and within browse/discovery views; placements must be swappable between house content and third-party ad network (e.g. Google AdMob) without UI rebuilds • Modular map/globe component — the map view must be built as a fully modular component so that multiple independent map instances can be added later (e.g. a separate map layer for partner businesses, local deals, or events) without rearchitecting the core feature • Premium user tier support — the user model must support a premium flag from day one; gating logic for features such as increased listing limits, promoted visibility, and boosted content must be implementable by flipping a config, not rewriting components • Business/partner account type — the user model must support a separate account type for businesses or organisations, distinct from individual user accounts, activatable post-launch • Promoted content slots — listings and profiles must support a promoted/sponsored flag in the data model so boosted content can be surfaced in feeds and discovery views without UI changes Technical Requirements We are open to React Native (Expo) or Flutter — we trust you to propose the framework you are most confident shipping great consumer apps in. What matters is the outcome, not the framework. The remaining tools below are strongly preferred and candidates should have direct experience with them or clear equivalents. Preferred stack (open to discussion) • React Native (Expo) or Flutter — we are open to either, single codebase for iOS and Android. Tell us which you recommend and why in your application. • Supabase — Postgres database, Auth, Realtime, and Storage • Supabase Realtime for live data sync (map pins, session status, chat) • Mapbox SDK or Google Maps SDK for the globe/map feature — Mapbox strongly preferred for globe rendering • Expo Notifications + OneSignal for push notifications • Stripe for payment architecture (integration required, activation deferred) • Clerk or Supabase Auth for Google and Apple sign-in Required experience • Minimum 3 published apps in the App Store or Google Play — links required in application • Prior experience building real-time features (live maps, chat, activity feeds) • Prior experience building consumer social or marketplace apps • Clean, maintainable, well-commented code — we will review code samples before hiring • Experience with App Store and Google Play submission and review processes • TypeScript preferred Engagement Terms This is a full-time engagement We are not looking for someone to work on this between other projects. We need a developer or team who will treat this as their primary focus for the duration of the build. We expect 35–40 hours per week minimum during the active build phase. Timeline • Active build phase: approximately 4–5 months • Post-launch maintenance and feature development: ongoing, long-term • We expect the winning candidate to be available for at least 12 months total Post-launch expectations • Bug fixes and OS compatibility updates as iOS and Android release new versions • App Store compliance updates as Apple and Google update policies • Feature additions on a rolling roadmap we will define together post-launch • Availability for urgent issues within 24 hours Preferred candidate type • Small agency (2–4 people) or a senior lead developer with a trusted sub-contractor network • Someone who has seen a project from zero to App Store before — multiple times • Fluent written English is required — you will be communicating with US-based founders daily How to Apply We receive a high volume of applications and filter aggressively. To be considered, your application must include all of the following. Applications missing any item will not receive a response. Required in your application • Links to at least 3 live apps you have built in the App Store or Google Play. Not screenshots, not videos — actual downloadable app links. • A brief description of the most technically complex app you have shipped and specifically what made it complex. • Your experience with Supabase Realtime specifically. If you have not used it, tell us what real-time tool you have used instead and why. • Your experience with map or globe integrations in a mobile app — Mapbox or Google Maps. Describe what you built. • Confirmation that you are available full-time and can begin within 2 weeks. • Your proposed hourly rate or monthly retainer for the build phase, and your expected rate for the ongoing maintenance phase. Please also include a proposed schedule of deliverables with estimated milestones and your projected timeline to completion. We expect weekly or biweekly check-in calls with the founding team and ask that you confirm you are available for these. • To confirm you have read this posting in full, begin your application with the phrase: “Mobile ready.” Applications that do not start with this phrase will not be reviewed. Shortlisting process: Top applicants will be invited to a 30-minute video call. Following the call, finalists will be given a small paid test task (compensated at your stated rate) before a final offer is made. We will not ask you to work for free at any stage. What We Offer • Competitive hourly rate or monthly retainer — we pay fairly for quality • Full product specification document and Figma designs provided on day one — no guessing what to build • Direct access to founders for fast decision-making — no corporate approval chains • Long-term relationship — if you do great work, you will have work for years • Milestone-based payments through Upwork escrow — protected for both sides • A genuinely interesting, well-scoped product with real market potential in a growing category We are serious founders building a serious product. We want a serious development partner. If that sounds like you, we look forward to hearing from you.

job_title: Senior Automation & Web Developer — Zapier / Airtable / APIs / WordPress / GTM / AI
description: About Us We're a fast-growing Australian business finance company. We're a lean team that competes through automation — our tech stack does the work of 100 people, and we're hiring one senior person to own, extend, and improve it full-time. (Company details shared with shortlisted candidates at interview stage.) This is NOT a VA role and NOT a junior dev role. You'll be the technical builder for the business, working directly with the owner (who built the current systems and knows them deeply — you won't be guessing alone). Our Stack (you'll work across most of this) -Zapier (advanced: code steps, webhooks, paths, error handling — not just simple Zaps) -Airtable (automations, scripting, complex base design, API) -Pipedrive CRM (API, webhooks, workflow automation) -ActiveCampaign (automations, API) -Python (Flask services deployed on Google Cloud Run) -REST APIs generally — reading API docs and building reliable integrations is the core of this job -LLM integrations (Claude / OpenAI APIs — building automations that use AI models via API) -WordPress — custom code (PHP/HTML/CSS/JS), performance optimisation (Core Web Vitals), and ongoing site management. Not just themes and plugins — you must be able to work in the code. -Google Tag Manager & tracking — GTM container setup, dataLayer coding, UTM parameter architecture, conversion tracking (including server-side / Conversions API) -Cloudflare, DNS, domains & hosting — DNS records, security settings, SSL, domain management (GoDaddy etc.), hosting environments -Softr (client portal on top of Airtable) -Plus: SMS APIs (Twilio/Sinch), Meta Conversions API, and AI voice APIs You don't need experience with every tool — but you MUST be strong on Zapier + Airtable + APIs + Python + WordPress (real coding, not just plugins), and able to learn the rest fast from documentation. What You'll Do -Build new automations and improve existing ones (lead routing, CRM workflows, client notifications, and LLM-powered automation systems) -Own our WordPress website end-to-end: performance (Core Web Vitals), custom code changes, design polish, and reliability -Own our tracking infrastructure: GTM, dataLayer, UTM architecture, and conversion tracking accuracy across Meta and Google -Manage the infrastructure layer: Cloudflare, DNS, domains, hosting, SSL, and security settings -Innovate with AI. We use LLMs heavily across our systems and expect you to stay current with new models, tools, and techniques — and to proactively propose where AI can improve or replace existing processes. "I saw this new capability and built a prototype" is the energy we pay bonuses for. -Debug production issues by finding root causes — not patching symptoms -Integrate third-party APIs by reading official documentation carefully and verifying exact parameter specs (this is a hard requirement for us — guessing at API parameters is how systems break) -Write clear documentation: every automation you ship comes with a written spec and runbook. No exceptions. -Proactively identify problems and improvements before being asked — we pay bonuses specifically for this Compensation -Base: USD $2,500–3,000/month depending on experience -Monthly performance bonus: USD $300–800 based on shipped systems that run reliably, documentation quality, and -proactive problem-finding. Opportunity to go even higher, based on performance. -Annual base increases for strong performers -Long-term, stable, full-time role — we are building for years, not months Hours Of Work Full-time, Monday–Friday, working - 9am - 6pm SYDNEY TIME. Who This Role Suits -5+ years building automations, integrations, and websites professionally — you're a senior generalist who's comfortable owning the entire technical surface of a business, not a specialist in one tool -You're a problem solver and have a high degree of attention to detail -You chase root causes, not symptoms — "I found why it breaks" instead of "I added a workaround" -You read API documentation for fun (or at least without pain) -You're genuinely excited by AI — you already use LLMs in your own workflow, follow new releases, and have built things with -AI APIs because you wanted to, not just because a client asked -You test your own work before calling it done -You communicate clearly and proactively — if something is blocked or broken, we hear it from you first -You want one stable long-term client who pays well and pays bonuses, not five gigs Who This Role Does NOT Suit -Anyone whose Zapier experience is limited to simple two-step Zaps -Anyone whose WordPress experience is page builders only (Elementor/Divi) — if you can't work directly in PHP/HTML/CSS/JS and diagnose performance issues in the code, this isn't your role -Anyone who hardcodes credentials or guesses at API parameters instead of checking docs -Anyone juggling multiple clients (we require exclusivity during work hours) -Agencies, teams, or anyone planning to subcontract any part of this work. We are hiring you, one individual — the person we interview is the person who does the work, always. Given the financial data our systems handle, subcontracting is treated as a serious breach and grounds for immediate termination. -Anyone uncomfortable with logged/audited system access — we run strict security practices (scoped credentials, audit trails). Honest builders find this boring; that's the point. Security Note (read this — it matters) We work with financial data, so we follow least-privilege access practices: you'll use your own named accounts and scoped API keys, production credentials are managed by the owner, and system activity is logged. This is standard, professional, and protects you as much as us. If that sounds reasonable, we'll get along great. SKILL REQUIREMENTS Required: -Zapier (Expert) -Airtable (Expert) -AI Tool Use — Claude Code / ChatGPT (Expert) -API Integration / REST APIs (Expert) -WordPress — custom code & performance (Advanced) -Google Tag Manager / UTM / conversion tracking (Advanced) -Python (Advanced) -HTML / CSS / JavaScript (Advanced) -Webhooks (Advanced) -Cloudflare / DNS / domain & hosting management (Intermediate–Advanced) Strongly preferred: -Pipedrive or similar CRM (HubSpot, Salesforce) -ActiveCampaign or similar (Mailchimp, Klaviyo) -Google Cloud Platform (Cloud Run, Cloud Functions) -Flask or similar Python web frameworks -Meta Conversions API / server-side tracking Nice to have: -Softr / no-code app builders -Twilio / Sinch / Kixie, SMS APIs -SQL HOW TO APPLY To apply, send a message that includes ALL of the following — applications missing any item will not be read: 1. Start your message with the word "PINEAPPLE" so we know you read the full post. 2. Your 2–3 best automation/integration projects — for each: what it did, which tools/APIs were involved, and one problem you hit and how you solved it. Specific detail matters more than polish. Include links wherever possible — live websites you've built or optimised, GitHub, portfolio, or Loom walkthroughs. Claims we can verify are worth far more than claims we can't. 3. Answer this question: A Zapier webhook step is receiving data from a third-party API, but one field arrives blank for about 4% of records even though the source system shows the data exists. Describe, step by step, how you would diagnose this. (There is no single right answer — we're looking at how you think.) 4. Answer this question: A WordPress landing page scores poorly on Core Web Vitals (high CLS, slow LCP) and its Meta conversion tracking is undercounting leads. Briefly: what are the first things you'd check for each problem? 5. Your expected monthly salary in USD. 6. Confirm you can work 9:00am–6:00pm Sydney time (including the earlier Manila start during Australian daylight saving) full-time and exclusively. 7. A short video introduction (3–5 minutes, camera on) — Loom or similar. Briefly: who you are, what you've built that you're proudest of, and what specifically about this role appeals to you. No script needed, no editing, no polish — we just want to meet the actual person we'd be talking to every morning. If you're selected, we'll contact you back to arrange a quick interview to see if we're a good fit to work together.

title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer (AI-Native)
description: I'm Connor, founder of AdStream. I'm based in Australia and I run this company small and fast. AdStream manages the ad creative workflow for e-commerce brands running creator-made (UGC) video ads at volume: creative briefs go out, creators upload video, the brand's team reviews and approves everything in the browser, and approved ads publish straight to Meta. See it for yourself before you apply. Make an account at ---------- , click around, poke at the brief and review flows. The best applications come from people who've actually touched the product. What we're building right now Video playback. Reviewers play and scrub large creator videos in the browser, and right now playback is laggy. We serve full-quality source files straight from S3, so reviewers wait on buffering instead of reviewing. The route forward is Drive-first: Google Drive becomes the home for every customer asset. That gets us three things at once, fast playback on large files, customer assets living in their own Google Drive (a place they control and a brand they already trust), and the foundation for semantic search. That last one is the exciting part: once every file lands in Drive, we process it, get the transcript and text embeddings so you can search what's said in a video, frame embeddings so you can search what's visually in it. "Find b-roll with a kettle on a table." "Pull every clip where someone says sustainable." Internal teams find images, b-roll and past ads in seconds instead of scrubbing through folders, which makes video editing and graphic design dramatically faster. Beyond that, the roadmap you'd own: deepening the Meta integration and adding TikTok (OAuth, campaign publishing, status webhooks), AI creative generation with OpenAI, and Stripe billing. The stack Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + React 19 + TypeScript. Tailwind v4. Supabase — Postgres with row-level security, auth, storage. AWS S3. Google Drive API. Meta Graph API. OpenAI. Deployed on Vercel. You don't need prior experience with every line, but be honest about which parts you haven't touched, and don't propose a rewrite in week two. This is an AI-native role We provide a paid Claude Code seat and cover your AI tooling. You must already work this way daily, agentic tools (Claude Code, Cursor or equivalent), not autocomplete. You can write a spec an agent can execute, review agent output critically instead of trusting it, and verify AI-written code before it ships. One senior with a real agentic workflow now ships what a small team shipped a few years ago, that's the bet this role is built on. How we work: A 10–20 minute call every morning: what's planned today, review of yesterday, check in on deadlines. We agree on milestones upfront so everyone stays accountable. Be upfront about how long things will take. Not so we can micromanage, so we can be honest with our users and set expectations they can trust. Don't tell us it's a day if it's a week. Own outcomes, not tasks. Questions early, blockers immediately. Async outside the morning call: Looms, written updates. Hours are 9am–5pm AEST — a normal 7am–3pm day shift in the Philippines, evenings free. How to apply: Start your application with the exact phrase "Drive-first." It tells me you actually read this. Record a Loom (5 minutes max — clear and tight beats thorough and rambling) covering: You and your work. Quick intro, then walk me through something real you've shipped, what it does and what you built. AI doing meaningful work. One real example of using an agent for something substantial: how you directed it, something it got wrong that you caught, and how you verified it before shipping. I want to see judgment, not AI slop. How AI changed your workflow. How much more do you ship now? Do you still write most lines by hand, or mostly review and direct? Your models. Which model do you prefer and why? Do you run more than one, and how do you split work between them? If your Loom lands, we'll jump on a call. Looking forward to hearing from you!

description: Technical Lead / Software Architect Real Estate Data, CRM & AI Automation Platform Remote | Contract, Part-Time, or Full-Time Preferred Regions: Ukraine, Eastern Europe, India, Philippines, Vietnam, or other experienced remote development markets Time Zone Requirement: Must have regular overlap with U.S. Eastern Time About the Company We are building a real estate data and lead generation platform for internal business use. The platform will combine property records, owner information, contact data, CRM history, public data sources, lead scoring, campaign workflows, and AI-assisted recommendations into one centralized operating system. The purpose of the platform is to help identify real estate opportunities, organize leads, prioritize follow-up, support outreach campaigns, and track business outcomes across multiple real estate-related services. This is not a basic website or a simple chatbot. This is a data-driven internal software platform with CRM, dashboard, automation, and AI components. We are looking for a Technical Lead / Software Architect who can help turn the business requirements into a practical, scalable technical plan and guide the development team through the first MVP and future phases. Platform Overview The platform will support several real estate business workflows, including: Property acquisition leads Off-market owner opportunities Distressed property leads Rental and leasing opportunities Property management opportunities Renovation and repair opportunities Insurance-related property events Financing and loan opportunities Legal and public-record-driven opportunities The system will collect and organize property and owner data, classify leads into the correct business category, score opportunities, display them in a dashboard, support CRM follow-up, and eventually power AI-assisted workflows. Role Overview We are hiring a Technical Lead / Software Architect to help design the foundation of the platform and oversee the technical direction of development. This person will work closely with the founder and development team to define the architecture, database structure, backend APIs, frontend requirements, AI integration plan, development roadmap, and engineering workflow. The right candidate should be able to understand both technical systems and business workflows. We need someone who can take a large product vision and break it into a practical, organized MVP that can be built, tested, and improved. This role may begin as part-time or contract-based, with the possibility of becoming a long-term leadership role. Key Responsibilities Translate business requirements into technical architecture Define the MVP scope and development priorities Design the database structure for properties, owners, contacts, CRM activity, source tracking, lead categories, and opportunity scoring Define backend API requirements Plan the frontend dashboard structure Design the AI assistant integration approach Help select the appropriate technology stack Create a 30-day, 60-day, and 90-day technical roadmap Break development into clear tasks for frontend, backend, data, and AI developers Review code, architecture decisions, and database design Set up or improve GitHub workflow, branches, pull requests, and development standards Help evaluate developers and review paid test tasks Prevent disconnected development between frontend, backend, data, and AI components Identify technical risks early Help d ---------- what should be built now versus later Communicate clearly with a non-technical founder Core Modules to Architect The initial platform will include: 1. Data Management Import real estate data from CSV, Excel, APIs, and future public data sources Clean and normalize property, owner, company, contact, and CRM data Track the source of each record Support deduplication and relationship mapping 2. Property & Owner Profiles Property detail pages Owner and company detail pages Contact information Related properties Public record indicators CRM history Notes, activity, and follow-up status 3. Lead Classification Assign properties and owners to relevant lead categories Support multiple opportunity types per property Create queues for different business workflows Track lead status and next action 4. Opportunity Scoring Score leads based on available data Consider motivation signals, urgency, property condition, public records, CRM activity, and estimated revenue potential Display clear reasoning behind scores 5. CRM & Campaign Workflow Track calls, SMS, email s, notes, and follow-ups Manage lead status Support campaign planning Prepare for future SMS, email , voi cemail , and calling integrations 6. AI Assistant Layer Generate property summaries Summarize owner and company information Review CRM history Recommend next actions Generate SMS, email , and call script drafts Explain why a lead may be an opportunity Highlight risks or missing information Use only available data and avoid unsupported assumptions 7. Dashboard & Reporting Dashboard overview Lead categories Lead sources Opportunity queues Recent alerts AI insights Revenue tracking Data quality reporting First MVP Goal The first MVP should prove the core workflow: Data Import ? Clean Database ? Property Profile ? Lead Category ? Opportunity Score ? Dashboard Queue ? AI Recommendation ? Follow-Up Action Within the first phase, the system should allow us to: Import sample real estate data Store clean property, owner, contact, and CRM records View records in a dashboard Search and filter leads Open property and owner profiles See CRM timeline and source trace Classify leads into business categories Generate AI-assisted summaries and next-action recommendations Track lead status and potential revenue category The first version does not need to include every integration or automation. It must create a clean technical foundation that can support future growth. Required Experience Strong software architecture experience Backend development experience Database design experience PostgreSQL experience REST API design Python and/or Node.js experience Understanding of React / Next.js applications Experience building SaaS platforms, CRMs, dashboards, marketplaces, internal tools, or data-heavy applications Experience working with structured data Experience reviewing code and managing development standards GitHub experience Ability to break complex projects into clear development milestones Strong communication skills Ability to work independently and take ownership Preferred Experience Real estate software experience CRM or lead management platform experience Public records or property data experience Data engineering or ETL experience AI / OpenAI API / LLM application experience Workflow automation experience SMS, email , or calling automation experience GoHighLevel, FreedomSoft, Podio, HubSpot, Salesforce, or similar CRM experience Docker or cloud deployment experience AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, Railway, Render, or Vercel experience Experience managing remote developers Experience building MVPs for startups or internal business platforms Ideal Candidate The ideal candidate can take a broad business idea and turn it into a clear technical plan. You should be able to answer questions such as: What should we build first? What should wait until later? How should the database be structured? How should property, owner, contact, and CRM records connect? How should the backend serve the dashboard? How should AI features safely use platform data? How should lead categories and scoring work? How should developers divide the work? What are the risks if we build this incorrectly? We are looking for someone practical, organized, and serious. We do not need theory. We need leadership, architecture, and execution. What We Are Not Looking For Please do not apply if: You only build basic websites You only work on frontend design You only do AI prompting without software architecture You cannot design database structure You cannot review other developers’ work You cannot communicate technical decisions clearly You prefer overbuilding instead of delivering a focused MVP You are not comfortable working in an early-stage environment You cannot take ownership of the technical direction How to Apply Please send: Resume or LinkedIn profile GitHub profile or portfolio Examples of platforms, CRMs, SaaS applications, dashboards, marketplaces, or internal tools you helped build Description of your backend architecture experience Description of your PostgreSQL / database design experience Experience working with React / Next.js teams Experience with AI, OpenAI API, automation, or LLM applications, if any Experience with real estate, public data, CRM, or lead generation systems, if any Experience managing or reviewing developers Hourly rate or monthly salary expectation Availability and preferred working hours Location and time zone A short explanation of how you would approach the first 30 days of this project Subject Line: Technical Lead / Software Architect – Real Estate Data & AI Platform Compensation Compensation depends on experience, availability, and engagement type. We are open to: Part-time technical lead Full-time technical lead Fractional CTO Software architect Contract-to-hire Long-term remote role Final Note We are looking for a serious technical leader who can help build the foundation of a real software platform. This role is important because the platform will involve data engineering, CRM logic, dashboard development, backend APIs, lead scoring, AI-assisted recommendations, campaign workflows, and future automation. We need someone who can bring structure, discipline, and technical leadership to the project from the beginning.

title: Creative Product Developer & Manager
description: CREATIVE PROJECT MANAGER (REMOTE) We run two growing consumer product brands - one in men's socks, the other in fun, novelty golf gifts - selling across the UK, USA and Australia on Amazon and on our own Shopify stores. Right now we have more good product ideas than we have hands to build them. That's where you come in. We're looking for a Creative Project Manager to own a FMCG PRODUCT's journey from idea to launch: take a concept, turn it into a physical sample, take it into production at the factory, and then make it look brilliant everywhere it's sold online. You'll be the person who makes things happen - not the person who waits to be told what to do. This is a creative, brand-led role, not a box-ticking project manager role. We need taste, initiative, and a real eye for what "good" looks like. WHAT YOU'LL DO • Take product ideas from concept through to physical samples • Brief and coordinate freelancers, designers and suppliers to get exactly the result you want • Commit products to production and drive them through to launch • Make our products look fantastic online - across Shopify, Amazon, wholesale and social • Spot gaps and opportunities to improve existing listings and the wider business •Run small experiments and improvements (for example, testing product images) • Present options and make decisions - keep things moving forward without being chased WHAT WE NEED FROM YOU (must-haves) • Strong DTC / Shopify experience - this is the single most important thing. You understand how to merchandise and present products in an online store and make them sell. • Great taste and style - you care how things look and sweat the details • A proven ability to take a product from idea to reality • You work well with freelancers and can direct creative work clearly to get the outcome you want • Proactive and self-driven - you see what needs doing and do it • Excellent written English and clear communication • Reliable, organised, and able to own projects end to end while working remotely OTHER EXPERIENCE • Amazon selling or listing experience • Experience with consumer goods, novelty products, or fashion / apparel • Experience working with overseas suppliers (e.g. China) • A background that started in design or creative execution and grew into managing projects THE KIND OF PERSON WHO THRIVES HERE • You have vision - you see what's missing and how to make it better • You take pride in your work, but you know when something is good enough to ship • You're hungry to take on more and grow with the business • You enjoy ownership and the freedom that comes with a remote role THE DETAILS • Full-time, fully remote • We're a UK-based team - we'll need atleast 5 hours of daily overlap with UK working hours, but you'll largely manage your own schedule • A long-term role with genuine room to grow as the brands scale and we build new brands HOW TO APPLY We read every application properly, so help us see you're a great fit: 1. Start your message with the word "SAMPLE" so we know you read to the end. 2. Tell us briefly about a product or online store you've worked on — ideally something you took from an idea (or a rough state) to looking great online. 3. Share any links or examples of your work — Shopify stores, product listings, or a portfolio. In a line or two, tell us why this role appeals to you. We can't wait to meet someone who can take an idea and run with it.

title: Cold Email Specialist (Infrastructure + Copy + Deliverability, Full Stack) - Long-Term
job_title: Cold Email Specialist (Infrastructure + Copy + Deliverability, Full Stack) - Long-Term
description: Compensation: $600 to $1,000 USD per month based on what you can prove. Hours: 40 hours per week. Some overlap with Morocco, Dubai, and EU business hours required (Manila 3 PM to 11 PM works for us; flexible within that range). READ THIS FIRST This is not an entry-level role. We are not looking for someone who watched a "cold email in 2026" YouTube playlist and sent 200 email s from their Gmail. We are looking for someone who has built sending infrastructure from zero, run real campaigns at volume, kept domains healthy, and booked real meetings for a real business. If that's not you yet, this isn't your post. If your experience is "I wrote cold email copy for a client once" or "I managed a VA team that did outreach", stop reading. The tests will expose it in an hour. ABOUT RMD RMD is a digital marketing agency. Our team is distributed across Morocco and Dubai and works remote. Our primary client base is in Dubai and the GCC, with growing work across the EU and North Africa. We run SEO, paid ads, branding, and web development for service businesses, e-commerce stores, and B2B companies in 20+ countries. WHAT THIS ROLE IS You own our outbound email machine end to end. Not just the copy. Not just the sending tool. The whole stack: 1. Infrastructure: secondary domains, mailboxes, DNS, warmup, sending health 2. Data: sourcing lead lists, cleaning them, verifying them, segmenting them 3. Copy: short plain-text sequences that get replies, not opens 4. Operations: campaign builds, launch checklists, inbox management, meeting booking, weekly reporting We already run a multi-domain, multi-mailbox sending setup on Instantly with a live campaign program into the GCC. You will take it over, keep it healthy, and scale it: first for RMD's own client acquisition, then for client campaigns as we grow the service. If you only want to write copy and hand the "technical stuff" to someone else, this role isn't a fit. The technical stuff IS the role. Copy that never lands in the inbox is decoration. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Set up and maintain sending infrastructure: buy secondary domains, configure SPF / DKIM / DMARC, create mailboxes, set custom tracking domains, run warmup, monitor health scores - Source lead lists by niche, title, and country (Apollo, LinkedIn Sales Navigator + scraper, LeadRocks, or equivalent), with GCC and EU targeting - Clean and verify every list before upload: strip free email domains, dedupe, verify (Reoon, MillionVerifier, or equivalent), enrich missing fields, make the catch-all keep-or-cut call - Write 3-step plain-text sequences (opener, bump, breakup) with personalization variables that actually render, and iterate them on reply-rate data - Build and launch campaigns in Instantly: schedules in the prospect's timezone and work week (much of the GCC runs Sunday to Thursday, the UAE runs Monday to Friday), stop-on-reply, text-only, daily caps per mailbox, domain-clustering caps per recipient company - Diagnose deliverability problems before they kill a domain: bounce spikes, spam placement, blacklists, when to pause vs rotate vs retire a mailbox - Manage the reply inbox daily: triage, answer objections, push for the meeting, book it on the calendar, hand the warm lead to the CEO with context - Report weekly with the numbers that matter: delivered, reply rate, positive reply rate, meetings booked per 1,000 sends, infra health - Use AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude) as part of the daily workflow. AI is openly used in the agency, not as a shortcut to skip thinking - Communicate with the team in writing daily (email , ClickUp). Updates short, blockers raised early REQUIRED (WE WILL VERIFY ALL OF THIS) - 2+ years running cold email campaigns end to end. Sourcing to inbox to booked meeting. Not "I wrote sequences". Ran the machine. - 2 campaigns from the last 12 months you can walk through with numbers: niche, list size, total sends, reply rate, positive reply rate, meetings or sales calls booked. With platform screenshots (redact client names if NDA). We will dig into these on the test and the call. - You have built sending infrastructure from zero, yourself. Domains bought, DNS records configured (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), mailboxes created on Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, warmup run, custom tracking domain set. Be ready to explain each DNS record's job in plain words. - Instantly in production. Smartlead or lemlist accepted if you can map over fast, but you should know your way around a sending platform's campaign builder, schedules, account health, and code/variable view without a tutorial. - One deliverability save you can tell start to finish. A domain or mailbox that started burning (bounces, spam folder, health drop), what you checked, what the root cause was, what fixed it, and what the numbers did after. "I just slowed the sending" is not a save story. - List building in production. You have pulled targeted B2B lists by title + industry + country from Apollo, Sales Navigator + a scraper, LeadRocks, or equivalent, and you know why a narrow GCC query returns 9 results while the same query in the US returns 9,000. - Email verification workflow. You verify every list before upload, you know the difference between valid, invalid, catch-all, and unknown, and you can defend when a catch-all is worth the bounce risk. - Copy that gets replies. Short, plain text, one idea per email , specific CTA, follow-ups that bump instead of re-pitching. You can name your benchmark reply rate by market and what you change first when a campaign comes in under it. - Reply handling to booked meetings. You have personally worked an outbound inbox: objections, "send me more info", ghosting, and you have booked meetings from it. Outbound that ends at "positive reply" is half a job. - Cold email canon. You have studied at least 2 of: Nick Saraev, Alex Hormozi ($100M Leads, the outreach chapters), Eric Nowoslawski, Daniel Fazio, Jay Feldman. Name a principle from one of them and point to a campaign above where you used it. - English fluency at C1 or higher. Your email s read like a human wrote them, not a template engine. - Stable internet, quiet workspace, 40 hours per week available. If we struggle to find the profile at this exact bar, we may relax the experience minimum case-by-case. We will not relax the campaign-numbers + infrastructure + deliverability evidence floor. BONUS (NOT REQUIRED) - Clay (enrichment workflows, waterfall verification) - Google Postmaster Tools and inbox placement testing in production - B2B experience in GCC, EU, or US markets specifically - French (we have France and North Africa clients) - Light automation (Zapier, Make) for lead routing and reporting - LinkedIn outreach experience alongside email (multichannel sequencing) WHO WE HIRE - People who ship the work and don't disappear - People who want a long-term role, not a gig - People who can take direction in writing, push back when they think we're wrong, and own a deliverable end to end - People who can show their work, not just describe it WHAT WE OFFER - $600 to $1,000 USD per month based on what you can prove. Top of band reserved for candidates who hit every "Required" item with evidence. - Direct work with the CEO and a small team. Your campaigns ship for real in week one - Real growth, not lip service. This is a role you grow OUT of, not stagnate in. The path here is cold email specialist, then outbound lead, then head of a productized outbound service we sell to clients. If you stay 18 months, you should not be doing the same work you started with. - You get to do more, fast. As you prove yourself, you take on more: client campaigns, strategy calls, multichannel outbound, junior briefing. We don't ration responsibility. - We reward progress and skill expansion. Learn a new tool, ship a harder deliverable, hit a result the team didn't expect. When that happens, we adjust your pay and scope to match. A-players see significant raises (80%+) within the first year. We measure progress, not seat-time. - Performance bonus structure discussed after the first month - Async-first culture. If you do the work, you'll be left to do it Who this is NOT for: people who want to stay at their current level and improve slowly. We're hiring people who want to move forward. If "comfortable plateau" is your goal, this isn't the seat. HOW TO APPLY Send your application to ---------- with the subject: "Cold Email Specialist PH, [Your Full Name]" In your email , include: 1. A 2-paragraph intro: who you are and why this role fits. 2. 2 campaigns you ran in the last 12 months. For each: niche | list size | total sends | reply rate | positive reply rate | meetings booked. Attach platform screenshots (redact client names if needed). 3. Your infrastructure proof. One setup you built from zero: how many domains and mailboxes, which DNS records you configured, which warmup tool, how long before full sending volume. A screenshot of account health helps. 4. Your deliverability save story in 5-8 sentences: what broke, what you diagnosed, what fixed it, what the numbers did after. 5. Cold email canon answer. Of Saraev / Hormozi / Nowoslawski / Fazio / Feldman: who shaped your approach the most? In 3-5 sentences: which principle of theirs you actually use, and point to a campaign above where you used it. 6. Reading-proof. Start your email body with the line: RMD RMD. (Yes, exactly those two words on the first line. This is how we know you actually read the post.) 7. Your salary expectation in USD per month. 8. When you can start full-time. We read every application that follows the format above. Applications missing the campaign numbers, infrastructure proof, save story, canon answer, or the RMD RMD first line will not be reviewed. We are filtering hard on purpose. If we want to move you to the screening stage, we reply within 5 business days. If you don't hear from us in that window, your application wasn't a fit this round. We're a small team without a dedicated recruiter, so please don't chase. We respect your time enough to be honest about that.

title: AI Systems Operator and Automation Specialist
job_title: AI Systems Operator and Automation Specialist

title: Junior Web Developer – 76,000/month (Remote)
description: We are a private equity-backed company operating 27 businesses across medical, real estate, and consulting. We are looking for a highly skilled Full-Time Junior Web Developer who can build and scale web pages rapidly, with a strong eye for structure, speed, and quality. This role is primarily focused on web page production. The bulk of your work will be approximately 80-90% creating and duplicating web pages at a consistent, high pace (using a template). These include home pages, service pages, blogs, landing pages, and a large volume of geolocation-specific pages that we build for our growing portfolio of healthcare and real estate brands. So basically, you will build a custom template from a figma design and then build it on wordpress (elementor), you will then duplicate the template for multiple pages (different locations) and you would just change the text copies and images on those duplicated pages. This is not just a production role. We are building something significant and we want a developer who takes pride in doing the work well, learns fast, and grows with the team. We currently have a team of 25+ talented Philippines-based developers, SEOs, and marketing professionals working across multiple US healthcare and real estate brands. You will be joining a high-performing, remote-first team that ships real work every day. WHY WORK WITH US We are a fast-growing organization with genuine long-term opportunities for the right people. Here is what sets us apart: •Above-market salary - At $1,250 USD/month (76,000 PHP), this role pays significantly above the Philippine market rate for a junior developer, and compensation grows as you do. •Real career development - You will work across 27 businesses in different industries, building skills in healthcare, real estate, and digital marketing that few developers your level get exposure to. •Stable, long-term work - This is not a project-based or short-term contract. We invest in the people on our team and we are looking for someone who wants to grow with us for years. •AI-forward team - We actively embrace AI tools to work smarter and faster. You will be encouraged and supported in using Claude AI and other tools to level up your output. •Leadership that understands digital - Our team is led by experienced digital marketing and SEO professionals who know the work from the inside. You will be supported, not just assigned tasks. •Remote and flexible - Work from anywhere in the Philippines with a stable internet connection. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY — PAGE PRODUCTION (80–90%) The core of this role is speed and consistency in web page production. title: Data Engineer – Platform Focus
description: Role Summary We are looking for a hands-on Data & AI Platform Infrastructure Engineer to build, secure, automate, and operate the infrastructure that supports our reporting, analytics, and AI initiatives. The core need is an engineer who can take ownership of the platform work required to make our data and AI environment secure, reliable, auditable, and scalable: identity and access integration, Snowflake administration and security, network and connectivity controls, data integrations and pipelines, monitoring and operational automation, and controlled implementation of approved AI capabilities. This role will reduce reliance on a single internal technical owner by establishing repeatable, documented, secure operations and taking day-to-day responsibility for technical implementation and maintenance. The person in this role will help ensure that the right people and services have the right access, that integrations and pipelines run reliably, that platform changes are auditable, and that new AI or data services are evaluated and implemented responsibly. Key Responsibilities 1. Identity, Access, and Snowflake Security •  Design, implement, and maintain Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) integration with Snowflake, including SSO and automated user/group provisioning where appropriate. •  Implement and maintain group-based role assignment, least-privilege RBAC, service-user access, key-pair authentication, warehouse access, onboarding, offboarding, and periodic access reviews. •  Maintain a clear role hierarchy and privilege model that separates administration, transformation, reporting, automation, and sensitive-data access. •  Configure and maintain masking policies, row-access controls, tags/classification, secure views, or related Snowflake governance controls as required. •  Produce access documentation and audit evidence showing who can access sensitive data and why. 2. Network Security, Platform Configuration, and Operations •  Configure, test, and maintain Snowflake network rules and network policies, IP allowlists, integration connectivity, authentication controls, and related security settings. •  Troubleshoot failed logins, blocked network connections, broken integrations, authentication problems, role/privilege issues, and platform operational failures. •  Establish repeatable deployment and change-management procedures for security and infrastructure configuration. •  Configure operational monitoring, alerts, cost/resource controls, runbooks, and maintenance procedures for the platform. •  Support security reviews, audit requests, i ---------- investigation, remediation tracking, and evidence collection. 3. Data Integrations, ETL/ELT, and Reliability •  Configure, maintain, and monitor data ingestion and integration pipelines into Snowflake, including existing and new vendor/system integrations. •  Evaluate integration options, authentication methods, data exposure, logging, failure handling, retry behavior, and operational support requirements. •  Build or maintain scripts and automations for pipeline monitoring, validation, alerting, recovery, auditing, and recurring platform administration. •  Work with dbt and downstream analytics processes as needed to ensure the underlying platform, credentials, environments, and deployments are dependable. •  Identify fragile, manual, or high-risk platform processes and implement sustainable improvements. 4. Documentation, Governance, and Team Enablement •  Build and maintain technical documentation, architecture diagrams, inventories, security baselines, implementation records, standard operating procedures, and troubleshooting runbooks. •  Document platform decisions, permissions, service accounts, authentication methods, integrations, scheduled jobs, monitoring, and recovery procedures. •  Translate recurring platform work into reusable scripts, checklists, templates, and automated controls. •  Communicate changes, risks, blockers, test results, and recommendations clearly to technical and nontechnical stakeholders. •  Partner with internal leadership, IT/security, and compliance stakeholders on approvals and risk decisions; this role implements and documents controls but is not the final legal or HIPAA compliance authority. Initial Priorities The initial priorities for this role are expected to include: •  Inventorying current Snowflake roles, users/service identities, warehouses, network/security policies, integrations, pipelines, scheduled jobs, and existing documentation. •  Developing and implementing a Microsoft Entra ID-to-Snowflake access-management approach, including group-to-role mapping, provisioning/deprovisioning procedures, and access-review evidence. •  Reviewing Snowflake security posture, including network rules/policies, authentication, masking/data access controls, service identities, secrets/key rotation, logging, alerts, and audit readiness. •  Establishing operational monitoring and runbooks for integrations, pipelines, security configuration, and platform failures. •  Establishing a controlled process for evaluating and enabling Snowflake AI capabilities and other AI-enabled services in a healthcare/HIPAA-regulated environment. •  Automating recurring administrative, audit, monitoring, and troubleshooting activities wherever practical and safe. "working on it" with assignee ? "completed by") Calendar wired to family + candidate portals (per-member read-only OAuth) Job board status synced to search stage with manual override A Resources tab (internal vs. client), with internal resources view-only/no-download, and resources auto-tagged to a client's profile based on their situation Records page, recycle bin/soft-delete, stage history & audit logging (largely designed) Integrations (bigger lifts) Email : a transactional + marketing service (Resend / Postmark / SendGrid) — redesigned stage-based templates and segmented blasts Video in-platform for interviews; AI transcripts attached to the right candidate record (Done already: a VideoAsk link for the Fast Track intro step) Mobile apps — App Store & Google Play Publish the platform to both stores (e.g., wrapping the web app with Capacitor), with push notifications Configure payments to pass store review (our memberships pay for a real-world service, generally exempt from Apple IAP — Stripe must stay within guidelines) Quality & scale Fast, smooth, simple. Clean schema, proper indexing, no hard cap on users. Documented, maintainable code. Required experience Strong JavaScript and front-end development Supabase or Postgres — Auth, Row-Level Security, SQL, Edge/serverless functions Stripe — especially Stripe Connect (payouts, transfers, webhooks), plus Elements, Invoicing, and ACH debit.
